title: Lissity under finite étale pushforward
statement: Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\neq p$ and an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$. Let $X_0,Y_0$ be separated $k_0$-schemes of finite type [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], let $g_0:Y_0\to X_0$ be a finite étale $k_0$-morphism [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and let $g:Y\to X$ be its geometric fibre over $k$. Let $\mathcal F$ be a lisse Weil sheaf on $Y_0$: a constructible $\Qlb$-Weil sheaf $(\mathcal F,\theta)$ on $Y_0$ [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex] whose underlying sheaf on $Y$ is a lisse $\Qlb$-sheaf [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves]. Then the direct image $g_*\mathcal F=Rg_*\mathcal F$ [def-weil-derived-direct-image], with the Weil structure of its equivariant lift [prop-weil-operations], is a lisse Weil sheaf on $X_0$ in the same sense: a constructible $\Qlb$-Weil sheaf on $X_0$ whose underlying sheaf on $X$ is a lisse $\Qlb$-sheaf.

source.place: opening proof sentence: the lissity on W of the finite étale pushforward

proof.text: Choose a finite coefficient field $E\subset\Qlb$ and a lisse $E$-sheaf $F_E$ representing the underlying sheaf $\mathcal F$, using [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves](4). The scheme $Y$ is of finite type over the Noetherian scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$, hence Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]; being covered by finitely many spectra of Noetherian rings, its underlying space satisfies the ascending chain condition on open subsets. So there are finitely many open-and-closed connected components of $Y$, by [lem-sfb-noetherian-connected-components-open]. On each nonempty component, [cor-galois-lisse-representations](2) identifies $F_E$ with a continuous finite-dimensional representation of its profinite fundamental group. By [lem-pod-profinite-stable-lattice], choose an invariant finite free $\mathcal O_E$-lattice; the same equivalence gives its lisse integral system $(M_n)_n$, with $M_n$ locally free of finite rank over $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ and $M_{n+1}\otimes_{A_{n+1}}A_n\cong M_n$. (The stalk of $M_n$ at the base point is $\Lambda/\varpi_E^n\Lambda$, free over $A_n$, by the transition isomorphisms; on a connected component the isomorphism class of the stalks of a locally constant sheaf is constant, the locus where it is a given class being open and closed, so every local value of $M_n$ is free.) Assemble these systems over the finitely many components. Via [lem-sf-proetale-locally-constant-origin] regard the levels on the pro-etale site. By [lem-sfb-integral-lisse-reduction-equivalence], their inverse limit $M$ is locally finite free over the completed coefficient ring, with $M/\varpi_E^nM\cong M_n$. This is the integral realization of the chosen lattice and represents $F_E$ after rationalization. No Frobenius-stable lattice is required: the lattice is chosen only for the underlying geometric sheaf.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(1), pp. 59-60; also Stanford L19, Proposition 1.1.9, p. 3

proof.text: The geometric-fibre map $g$ is finite and etale: finiteness is stable under base change by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence](a), and etaleness by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits](1). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-etale-etale-local-split] at every point of $X$. This gives an etale covering family $u:U\to X$ with $Y_U=Y\times_XU\cong\coprod_{j\in J_U}U$, where $J_U$ is finite and may be empty; write $t_j:U\to Y$ for the sheet maps. Work separately on these covering members; a single global constant degree or a globally split cover is not assumed.

For an $A_n$-module sheaf $G$ on $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$, compute direct image on the slice over a splitting member $U$. By [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] this is restriction to $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$. For an object $V\to U$, [def-weil-proetale-module-direct-image] gives $(g_*G)(V)=G(Y\times_XV)=\prod_{j\in J_U}(t_j^*G)(V)$: the second equality is the sheaf axiom for the finite disjoint clopen covering of $Y\times_XV$. These equalities respect restrictions and scalar multiplication coordinate by coordinate, so $(g_*G)|_U\cong\prod_j t_j^*G$. Each $t_j$ is etale, and its restriction functor is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-restriction-injectives]. A finite product preserves kernels componentwise and preserves epimorphisms: locally lift each of the finitely many coordinates, then take a common refinement of their covering families. Thus the displayed finite product is exact. Exactness can be checked on the covering family $U\to X$ by local lifting of sections, so $g_*$ on these constant-coefficient module sheaves is exact.

source.place: Proof of Tag 095B, lemma-pushforward-locally-constant: localization and finite-product calculation

proof.text: Set $N_n=g_*M_n$ at finite coefficient level. The exact-functor theorem [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor] and step 3 give $Rg_{*,n}M_n\cong N_n[0]$. On the etale site, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-finite-pushforward-locally-constant] gives a finite locally constant module sheaf $g_*M_n^{\mathrm{et}}$. Its pro-etale pullback is $N_n$: on a splitting member the etale finite-exchange isomorphism [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-exchange] and the calculation of step 3 both identify the canonical comparison with the same finite product of the pulled-back sheet restrictions. The comparison is the identity in every coordinate, so these local identifications glue. Moreover $N_n$ is locally finite free over $A_n$: on a splitting member refine the finitely many locally free sheet trivializations, and the product becomes a finite direct sum of finite free modules. Tensoring this finite sum with $A_n$ gives $N_{n+1}\otimes_{A_{n+1}}A_n\cong N_n$. The isomorphism is induced by the pushed transition map, since its $j$-th coordinate is exactly the transition map on the $j$-th sheet. This also proves compatibility with successive reductions. All transition maps are epimorphisms.

source.place: Tag 095B, lemma-pushforward-locally-constant; Tag 0959, lemma-finite-pushforward-commutes-with-base-change; Derived Categories Tag 015F

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-integral-lisse-reduction-equivalence] to $(N_n)_n$: $N=\varprojlim_nN_n$ is locally finite free over $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}$ with reductions $N/\varpi_E^nN\cong N_n$. The corresponding etale tower from step 4 is a lisse $\mathcal O_E$-system in [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves](1). The pro-etale towers $(M_n)_n$ and $(N_n)_n$ have epimorphic transitions; [det-pe-milnor-epimorphic] therefore identifies their ordinary inverse limits with their derived inverse limits. For $M$ and $N$, ordinary reduction is also derived reduction: locally they are finite free completed-coefficient modules, so multiplication by $\varpi_E^n$ is injective and its cokernel is the indicated $A_n$-module; the two-term resolution of the quotient computes the derived tensor. Consequently the defining formula [def-weil-derived-direct-image] gives $Rg_*M=R\varprojlim_n Rg_{*,n}M_n\cong R\varprojlim_nN_n\cong N[0]$. The tower comparison is coherent because step 4 used the actual transitions. Also $g_*M=\varprojlim_ng_*M_n=N$ directly from the sectionwise formula [def-weil-proetale-module-direct-image], since inverse limits of sheaves are sectionwise. Thus the identification is with the underived direct image. For $P\in\{M,N\}$, with $P_n=P\otimes^L A_n=P/\varpi_E^nP$, the reduction map $c:P\to\prod_nP_n$ is injective with image $\varprojlim_nP_n=\ker(1-T)$ (by the equivalence above, $P\cong\varprojlim_nP_n$), and $1-T$ is an epimorphism by [det-pe-milnor-epimorphic]; this short exact sequence gives a Roos triangle with first map $c$, so $P$ is derived complete [def-weil-derived-complete]. Its reductions $P_n$ are locally constant with finite stalks in degree zero, constructible with the single stratum, uniformly in $n$; hence $P\in D^b_c(-,\mathcal O_E)$ with amplitude $[0,0]$. For $M$ this is the hypothesis of the defining formula used above; for $N$ it is the conclusion.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(1), p. 59; integral reconstruction and the finite-level definition of direct image

proof.text: Rationalize the isomorphism of step 5 and pass to the $\Qlb$ common-stage category, exactly as prescribed in [def-weil-derived-direct-image]. This gives $Rg_*\mathcal F=g_*\mathcal F$ represented by the lisse sheaf $(N\otimes E)\otimes_E\Qlb$ of [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves](2),(4). The finite-sheet formula also verifies the scalar-extension comparisons used here: for a finite coefficient-field extension, tensoring a finite direct sum of sheet restrictions gives the same sum after extension; each comparison is the identity on the extended coordinates, hence is compatible with transitions and composites of extensions. The output is bounded constructible and lies in degree zero, by step 5 and the rational/common-stage convention; hence it lies in the constructible heart [def-weil-constructible-heart]. This argument includes rank zero, a missing fibre (the empty product is the zero module), and disconnected schemes with varying degree and rank.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(1),(4), pp. 59-60; rational and common-stage conventions of the direct-image definition

proof.text: Finally apply [prop-weil-operations] to $Rg_*\mathcal F$ on the bounded constructible domain just proved. Its Weil isomorphism is $L\Phi_X^*Rg_*\mathcal F\xrightarrow{\mathrm{Ex}_*}Rg_*L\Phi_Y^*\mathcal F\xrightarrow{Rg_*\theta}Rg_*\mathcal F$. The hypothesis that $g_0$ is a $k_0$-morphism supplies its Frobenius compatibility; no continuity of an arithmetic Galois action is being imposed. The forgetful functor has the underlying direct image calculated in steps 5-6. Since that object is in the constructible heart and is lisse, [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex](3) makes this equivariant lift a constructible lisse Weil sheaf on $X_0$, as claimed.

source.place: Definition 1.1.7 and following paragraph, p. 2 (operations on Weil sheaves)

split_report.summary: Expanded the finite-etale lissity assertion by choosing geometric integral lattices, computing direct images as finite sheet products, checking quotient-transition compatibility, realizing the pushed tower, and only then applying the Weil equivariant lift. Reused existing nodes throughout; no new nodes and no statement change.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q147-fdb73d6b6 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read in full: the item and all 7 steps, the statement of each of the 22 cited nodes, the main-20261015 proof of lem-a1-reduction-lisse-pure, and the Stacks lemmas 04HN, 095B, 0959 and 015F. In the blueprint, lissity was only claimed through lem-a1-finite-map-purity, which proves purity alone, so this item fills a real gap. The statement is true and unchanged. Small cases checked: empty source or target, the identity, a split cover with sheets of different ranks, disconnected targets with varying degree, and the zero sheaf. Coefficient category: the steps keep the pro-etale D^b_c of def-weil-derived-direct-image and use the etale towers only for the def-pod lissity clause. Batch-5 check: cor-galois-lisse-representations (the lisse sheaf / pi_1-representation dictionary) and lem-pod-profinite-stable-lattice (stable lattice for a compact group) are general foundations. Their closures contain no trace-formula or Poincare-duality theorem node, and neither assumption leaf states or implies them. They are also genuinely needed, because a lattice taken straight from the definition can have torsion stalks, and then the levels are not locally free. Accepted. Two faults, fixed in fixes/dag/nodes/sec-deligne-laumon-a1/lem-a1-finite-map-lisse.json. (1) C1 in step 1: the Noetherian property of Y was used without a node, so I cited lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian, and I added why every local value of M_n is free. (2) E1/E3 in step 5: the claim that N is derived complete because its reductions are constructible does not follow, and the input M was never shown to lie in D^b_c(Y,O_E), which the definition of Rg_* requires. I replaced this with the Roos-triangle argument for both M and N (P is the limit of P_n, and 1-T is an epimorphism by det-pe-milnor-epimorphic), citing def-weil-derived-complete. The declared tool_uses are accepted. There are no new nodes, no duplicate found among about 10 candidate nodes, and no SGA source.; 1 file(s) fixed by the reviewer

lean.statement: theorem isLisse_lowerStar_of_isFiniteEtale (D : WeilConjectures.FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (hl : l ≠ D.p) {X₀ Y₀ : Scheme.{u}} [X₀.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of D.k₀))] [Y₀.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of D.k₀))] [IsSeparated (X₀ ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of D.k₀))] [IsSeparated (Y₀ ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of D.k₀))] [LocallyOfFiniteType (X₀ ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of D.k₀))] [QuasiCompact (X₀ ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of D.k₀))] [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y₀ ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of D.k₀))] [QuasiCompact (Y₀ ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of D.k₀))] (g₀ : Y₀ ⟶ X₀) [g₀.IsOver (Spec (CommRingCat.of D.k₀))] [IsFinite g₀] [Etale g₀] [QuasiCompact g₀] [QuasiSeparated g₀] [LocallyOfFiniteType g₀] [Fact (ringChar D.k₀ ≠ l)] (F : WeilSheaf D.k₀ l Y₀) (hF : F.IsLisse) : Nonempty ((WeilComplex.derivedLowerStar (k₀ := D.k₀) (l := l) g₀).obj (toComplex.obj F) ≅ toComplex.obj ((lowerStar g₀).obj F)) ∧ ((lowerStar g₀).obj F).IsLisse
